name: Avial
subtitle: Mixed vegetables bound in coconut, cumin and yogurt, finished with raw coconut oil

image.alt: An Onam sadya, the feast avial belongs to

ingredients.note: 2 for cooking, 1 raw at the end

prepNotes: Everything is cut to the same baton shape and size so it cooks evenly and looks right — this is not a dish where you cube things.
The final spoon of raw coconut oil is not optional. It is the smell of avial.

steps.text: Cook the vegetables hardest-first in a wide pan with turmeric, salt and just enough water — yam and banana first, softer vegetables after.
steps.tip: Barely enough water. Avial is not a curry and should not be swimming.

steps.text: Coarsely grind the coconut with cumin and green chilli. Do not make it a smooth paste.
steps.tip: Coarse. The texture of avial comes from the ground coconut.

steps.text: Fold the coconut mixture through the cooked vegetables and simmer 5 minutes.
Take the pan off the heat, then stir in the whisked yogurt. Return briefly to very low heat but do not let it boil.
steps.tip: Boiling after the yogurt goes in will split it.

steps.text: Crush the curry leaves between your palms and stir them in with the raw coconut oil.
Rest 10 minutes before serving. Avial is served warm, not hot.

storage: Keeps 2 days refrigerated. Reheat very gently — the yogurt splits over direct heat. Do not freeze.
